column1: # Cheap-lever tests on JSON.parse (json-only.js, 7,333,850-byte payload, 20 parses)

column5: the string cache is a net win: it reuses every string after the first parse, so dropping it allocates thousands of strings per parse
`compact_property_arenas`'s quicksort is not worth removing (and compaction keeps shapes tight)

a per-string `std::env::var_os` in the string path cost 5.9 ms/parse (7.8 -> 13.7): a per-string library call is not free, and the dedup experiment had to move its switch to a `OnceLock` before its numbers meant anything
neither cheap lever helps; the remaining costs are the scalar `parse_json_text` (43%) and allocation/GC (16%+), which need a structural/SIMD parser and allocation-free building, not a tuning change

column1: # Ceiling arithmetic for json-parse-inspector (from the same profile split)

column3: even if the scalar tokenizer (43%, 3.35 ms) became free, the remaining 4.44 ms would still be 1.18x slower than Bun's 3.77 ms; beating Bun by 1.5x needs 2.51 ms, i.e. tokenizing AND object building both near-free
column6: so no parser-only change can reach the bar on this row; it needs the builder (GC/alloc/dedup) cut ~2x at the same time
